findings.evidence: The author's own reply in the `reuse` thread demonstrates the mechanism for the sibling def: "`smulRange` is a `def` in a `public section` and is not `@[expose]`d, so its body is not available outside ... and the range API does not apply to `smulRange` there at all" (with the elaborator error `smulRange ↦ 763`). The general file bridges its own def this way (`smulRangeDirectSumEquiv_apply := (rfl)`, Module.lean:229); `vertexComponent` has no such lemma.
findings.fix: Add `theorem vertexComponent_eq_smulRange (v : Q) : vertexComponent k M v = smulRange k M (vertexIdempotent k v) := (rfl)`, and a vertex-level restatement of `coe_smulRangeDirectSumEquiv_symm_apply` (component of `x` at `v` is `eᵥ • x`). Do not `@[expose]` the body instead.
findings.issue: `vertexComponent` is a `def` in a `public section` with no `@[expose]`, so its body is unavailable downstream and no `smulRange` lemma applies to it. There is no `vertexComponent_eq_smulRange`/`_def` restatement, so `smulRange_le_comap`, `smulRangeDirectSumEquiv`, `smul_coeLinearMap` and — critically — `coe_smulRangeDirectSumEquiv_symm_apply` ("the component of `x` at `v` is `eᵥ • x`", the exact fact the roadmap's inversion of `quiverRepEquivalence` needs) are unreachable at the vertex level.

findings.evidence: Mathlib/Combinatorics/Quiver/Path.lean:196 `@[simp] lemma comp_toPath_eq_cons (p : Path a b) (e : b ⟶ c) : p.comp e.toPath = p.cons e`; :94 `@[simp] theorem comp_cons`.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] theorem pathMap_cons {a b c : Q} (p : Quiver.Path a b) (e : b ⟶ c) : pathMap k M (p.cons e) = (pathMap k M e.toPath).comp (pathMap k M p)`, provable from `pathMap_comp` and `Quiver.Path.comp_toPath_eq_cons`.
findings.issue: `pathMap_comp` is the only composition lemma, but its LHS `pathMap k M (p.comp q)` is unreachable for simp on concrete paths: Mathlib's `@[simp] Quiver.Path.comp_toPath_eq_cons` and `@[simp] Quiver.Path.comp_cons` rewrite `p.comp q` into `cons` form first, and there is no `pathMap` lemma matching `Quiver.Path.cons`. `pathMap k M (p.cons e)` is therefore stuck, even though `cons` is the form every path induction/destructuring produces.

findings.evidence: Grep of the file shows only `vertexComponentMap` (line 175), `coe_vertexComponentMap_apply` (182) and `vertexComponentMap_comp_pathMap` (189); no id/comp law. Contrast the path side, which does supply both `pathMap_nil` (148) and `pathMap_comp` (158).
findings.issue: `vertexComponentMap` is documented as "the morphism half of the passage from `kQ`-modules to representations of `Q`", but the two functoriality laws are missing: nothing states `vertexComponentMap k LinearMap.id v = LinearMap.id` or `vertexComponentMap k (g.comp f) v = (vertexComponentMap k g v).comp (vertexComponentMap k f v)`. Only `coe_vertexComponentMap_apply` and naturality against `pathMap` are given, so the assignment cannot be used as a morphism map without reproving them.

findings.evidence: Module.lean:88-89 `@[simp] theorem mem_smulRange_iff`; Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Submodule/Range.lean:67-68 `@[simp] theorem mem_range`. ModuleDecomposition.lean:99-102 has no attribute.
findings.fix: Tag `mem_vertexComponent_iff` with `@[simp]`; it is hypothesis-free (idempotency is discharged internally) and rewrites to the fixed-point form the whole file uses.
findings.issue: `mem_vertexComponent_iff` carries no `@[simp]`, although its general counterpart `mem_smulRange_iff` does (Module.lean:88) and Mathlib's `LinearMap.mem_range` does. Combined with the hidden body, `x ∈ vertexComponent k M v` has no simp support whatsoever downstream.

summary: The general `smulRange` API is complete and correctly bridged, but the path-algebra layer is not: `vertexComponent` has an unexposed body and no `= smulRange` restatement, so none of the general API reaches downstream consumers; `pathMap` has no `cons` lemma, so its `@[simp]` set is dead on the constructor form; and `vertexComponentMap` is missing the id/comp laws the file advertises as the morphism half of a functor.
